 "cells": [
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "jxgvokaN7HIS",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "# Introduction to Machine Learning"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "EjkL2cO47HIV",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "To apply today's course, we will analyze together examples of projects involving the development of Machine Learning algorithms. We will then see a complete case of ML including data cleaning, modeling and evaluation.\n",
    "\n",
    "Up to you! And remember, don't get stuck, search, ask questions, have fun! We are all here to learn and practice."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "hWlsKN5Y7HIV",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "## 1) Application case"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "VUyrPoby7HIW",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "In this exercise, you have minutes of kick-off meetings for projects involving machine learning. You need to determine:\n",
    "- Are we talking about a supervised or unsupervised problem?\n",
    "- Is the data structured or unstructured?\n",
    "- Is it a regression or classification problem? Neither of the two ?\n",
    "- What are the features and what is the target?\n",
    "- What other feature ideas do you have in mind for the given problem?\n",
    "\n",
    "Feel free to brainstorm as a group."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "iVUw5xnh7HIW",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "a) Sales prediction: The goal of the project is to predict the sales of a perfume shop to adjust the stock accordingly. The shop organizes events both in person and on social networks. Its sales are very sensitive to the season and the weather. The company can easily provide its sales data and the planning of its physical events, on the other hand we must go and retrieve the other information if necessary."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "1. Supervised\n",
    "2. Structured\n",
    "3. Regression \n",
    "4. Target: Chiffres de Vente / Features: Season, Weather, (historical sales data), Event type (In person, Social Network)\n",
    "5. Special/Unexpected Events (in further release)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "cxfj325p7HIW",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "b) Detection of the risk of default: The aim of the project is to detect if a person is at risk of not being able to repay his loan. This will save time to focus only on the most contentious cases. Loan data and subscriber data are already in the database."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "1. Supervised\n",
    "2. Structured (sales date), Unstructured / non existing (customers data)\n",
    "3. Classification\n",
    "4. Target: At risk or Not / Features: Loan data, Subscriber data\n",
    "5. Net Incomes, Debt %age, Address, Age, Sex, Contract Type"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "8vFDkrcE7HIW",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "c) Customer segmentation: The company delivers vegetable baskets. The goal of the project is to get to know their customers better by grouping them according to their characteristics. They will be able to think about how to improve the experience of each customer profile. They send us their basket sales data and we asked for whatever information they could have on their customers (in progress)."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "1. Unsupervised\n",
    "2. Structured\n",
    "3. Classification\n",
    "4. Target: Customer Type / Features: Sales data, customer data (not received yet)\n",
    "5. Genre, age, address, type (company, person)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "OdJrrWoF7HIW",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "d) Fracture diagnostics: The company is a radiology practice and wishes to have an algorithm for detecting the type of fracture. There are 7 types of fractures (transverse, longitudinal, displaced oblique, non-displaced oblique, greenstick, comminuted, spiral). From the radio, it is not always obvious and some are rare. This is why based on all the x-rays and their confirmed diagnoses, we want to develop an algorithm."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "1. Supervised\n",
    "2. Unstructured\n",
    "3. Classification\n",
    "4. Target: Fracture Type / Features: Historique de radios (radio + diagnostic)\n",
    "5. Caractéristiques de chaque type de fracture (vérifier si quantifiable avec les médecins)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "QXfexAei7HIX",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "## 2) Data Cleaning"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "HMKF4NoO7HIX",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "A jewelry company comes up with an idea to help sales associates identify customers with the highest purchasing potential. For this, according to their internal criteria, they were able to collect purchasing information from their customers and assign them a category between *occasional*, *frequent* and *vip* . Vip designates the most important customers, *frequent* the regulars and occasional the remaining customers.\n",
    "\n",
    "As a Data Analyst, you are asked to prepare data for the creation of a machine learning algorithm. Thus, for customers that are not yet categorized, it will suffice to use the algorithm to predict their categories and thus adapt the level of service accordingly."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "0xyg5mFD7HIX",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "#### Identifying the problem"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 450,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "# Import shared functions\n",
    "import sys\n",
    "import os\n",
    "shared_path = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), \"../Shared\"))\n",
    "if shared_path not in sys.path:\n",
    "    sys.path.append(shared_path)\n",
    "import functions"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "a) Download the `customer_segmentation.csv` file at this [address](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1vnwPLcHcsrbZScKEG8yD4oPOVUyGHDTB/view?usp=sharing) and load the data in a `df` variable"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "9EoTAHku7HIX",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "The data has 9 columns:\n",
    "- country: the customer's country of origin\n",
    "- client_type(customer_type): the importance category of the customer\n",
    "- average_basket: the average number of items purchased by the customer rounding up\n",
    "- average_price: the average price spent by the customer rounding up\n",
    "- visit_number: the number of visits made by the customer to the store\n",
    "- age: the age of the customer\n",
    "- gender: the customer's gender\n",
    "- hobbies: leisure activities declared by the client\n",
    "- customer_id: the internal unique identifier of the customer"
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "b) Qualify the type of machine learning problem you are facing and identify the features and the target variable."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "**Supervised classification** (assign one predefined category based on available features).<br>**Features:** country (qualitatif), average_basket (quantitatif), average_price (quantitatif), visit_number (quantitatif), age (quantitatif), gender (qualitatif) and hobbies(qualitatif)<br>**Target variable** to predict: client_type (qualitatif)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {

   "source": [
    "g) [more difficult] Delete rows whose `average_price` column values ​​are absurd in your opinion. Consider using panda masking techniques. **Be careful not to delete the null values ​​that we will then process** As a reminder, to determine the null values ​​of the column we can use `df.average_price.isnull()`"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 455,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "-1.0        231\n",
       " 191.0        1\n",
       " 197.0        1\n",
       " 206.0        2\n",
       " 209.0        1\n",
       "           ... \n",
       " 26014.0      1\n",
       " 26306.0      1\n",
       " 27383.0      1\n",
       " 27818.0      1\n",
       " 28137.0      1\n",
       "Name: average_price, Length: 5053, dtype: int64"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    },
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "len(df): 9000\n",
      "len(df_cleaned): 8305\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "display(df.average_price.value_counts().sort_index())\n",
    "# Delete rows with average_price = 0 or negative\n",
    "print(f\"len(df): {len(df)}\")\n",
    "mask = df.average_price > 0\n",
    "# Add .copy() to make sure that df_cleaned is a copy, not a view\n",
    "df_cleaned = df.loc[mask, :].copy()\n",
    "print(f\"len(df_cleaned): {len(df_cleaned)}\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "BgBcZ7Ag7HIZ",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "#### Handling missing values"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "i9SnhsRF7HIZ",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "h) To replace missing values, one must first ensure that they do not represent a large part of the data. Calculate the proportion of missing values ​​per column."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 456,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "country            0.000000\n",
       "client_type        0.000000\n",
       "average_basket     0.000000\n",
       "average_price      0.000000\n",
       "visit_number       0.000000\n",
       "age                2.059001\n",
       "gender             1.035521\n",
       "hobbies           90.114389\n",
       "dtype: float64"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "def display_missing_values_rate():\n",
    "    percent_missing = df_cleaned.isna().sum() * 100 / len(df_cleaned)\n",
    "    display(percent_missing)\n",
    "\n",
    "display_missing_values_rate()"
   ]
  },

    "id": "GfU5cJn47HIZ",

  {

   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "ZBaC6dPY7HIZ",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "k) What strategy(ies) can you consider to replace missing values ​​in the `average_price`, `age` and `gender` columns?"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "**average_price - age:** replace by the average value<br>**gender:** set to \"Unknown\""
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "0xEP6Kfi7HIZ",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "l) Replace the missing values ​​in the `gender` column with the mode. For that, see how to calculate mode and then parse pandas [fillna](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/stable/reference/api/pandas.DataFrame.fillna.html) function."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 459,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "2 possible values: ['female' 'male']\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "df_cleaned.gender.fillna(\n",
    "    value=df_cleaned.gender.mode()[0],\n",
    "    inplace=True,\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "functions.show_unique_values(df_cleaned.gender)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "w3-t_6Tr7HIZ",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "m) Replace the missing values ​​in the `average_price` and `age` columns with their respective means."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 460,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "df_cleaned.average_price.fillna(\n",
    "    value=df_cleaned.average_price.mean(),\n",
    "    inplace=True,\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "df_cleaned.age.fillna(\n",
    "    value=df_cleaned.average_price.mean(),\n",
    "    inplace=True,\n",
    ")"
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "#### Convert text to numeric columns"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "Dgj7_3kU7HIa",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "#### The target variable"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "5zMhUY3I7HIa",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "o) Transform `y` to values ​​0, 1 and 2 with sklearn's [LabelEncoder](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.preprocessing.LabelEncoder.html) tool. Check and view classes."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 463,
   "metadata": {
    "id": "K0qeyL3iesc5",
    "outputId": "a9ae259a-e921-4e34-cac5-5ceaef5fcd70"
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "array([1, 1, 1, ..., 1, 1, 1])"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    },
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "{0: 2009, 1: 5726, 2: 570}"
      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 463,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "\n",
    "le = LabelEncoder()\n",
    "le.fit(y.client_type)\n",
    "y = le.transform(y.client_type)\n",
    "display(y)\n",
    "\n",
    "unique, counts = np.unique(y, return_counts=True)\n",
    "dict(zip(unique, counts))"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "huaBDPjI7HIc",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "The classes are transformed by their index in alphabetical order, 0 for the first, 1 for the next ...."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "9FWzjj407HId",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "#### Features"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "zMTGdqBr7HId",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "p) In a new `X_dummy` variable, transform the text of the `country` and `gender` columns with the tool [OneHotEncoder](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.preprocessing/OneHotEncoder.html#sklearn.preprocessing.OneHotEncoder) from sklearn. Then display the categories. **Add sparse=False in parameters of OneHotEncoder()**"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 464,
   "metadata": {
    "id": "Dj0XxEpXesc5",
    "outputId": "21892ee1-7e6d-4f8f-cb04-9aee9911dc2a"
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "[array(['fr', 'it', 'uk'], dtype=object),\n",
       " array(['female', 'male'], dtype=object)]"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder\n",
    "\n",
    "# To only keep the qualitative features, only keep country and gender from the x DataFrame\n",
    "qualitative_features = x[[\"country\", \"gender\"]]\n",
    "encoder = OneHotEncoder(sparse_output=False)\n",
    "X_dummy = encoder.fit(qualitative_features)\n",
    "display(X_dummy.categories_)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "UzrkqqtW7HId",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "q) What does this statement do?"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 465,

   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "['fr' 'it' 'uk' 'female' 'male']\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "dummy_cols = np.concatenate((X_dummy.categories_[0], X_dummy.categories_[1]), axis=None)\n",
    "print(dummy_cols)"
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "#### Normalization"

  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "N5A_9NmH7HIe",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "Now that our data no longer contains any text type data, we will normalize our numeric features."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "rI2Vh2ru7HIf",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "s) In an `X_num` variable, normalize the values ​​of the `average_basket`, `average_price`, `visit_number` and `age` columns. You can use the [StandardScaler](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.preprocessing.StandardScaler.html) tool from sklearn."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 467,
   "metadata": {
    "id": "ptg7ceugesc6"
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler\n",
    "\n",
    "# To only keep the quantitative features, keep \"average_basket\", \"average_price\", \"visit_number\" and \"age\" from the x DataFrame\n",
    "quantitative_features = x[[\"average_basket\", \"average_price\", \"visit_number\", \"age\"]]\n",
    "scaler = StandardScaler()\n",
    "scaler.fit(quantitative_features)\n",
    "\n",
    "X_num = scaler.transform(x[[\"average_basket\", \"average_price\", \"visit_number\", \"age\"]])"
   ]
  },

    "id": "snp0focb7HIf",

    "- dummification of textual values ​​with labelencoder for target (client_type) and onehotencoder for features (country, gender)\n",
    "- normalization of numerical features (average_basket, average_price, visit_number, age)\n",
    "- concatenation of results in a single variable X"
   ]

   "source": [
    "from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier\n",
    "\n",
    "clf = DecisionTreeClassifier(random_state=42, max_depth=5)\n",
    "clf.fit(X_train, y_train)"
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "y_pred = clf.predict(X_test)\n",
    "dict_client_type_mapping = {\n",
    "    0: \"frequent\",\n",
    "    1: \"occasional\",\n",
    "    2: \"vip\",\n",
    "}\n",
    "values = [dict_client_type_mapping[pred] for pred in y_pred]\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f\"Training data accuracy : {clf.score(X_train, y_train)}\")\n",
    "print(f\"Test data accuracy : {clf.score(X_test, y_test)}\")"
   ]

    "## 4) Prediction"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {
    "id": "60n3SwV47HIh",
    "lang": "en"
   },
   "source": [
    "x) Download the file `customer_segmentation_new.csv` at this [address](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1dbveJ9Urk7KQ4RaDynXD4wKLpNZ6U6yY/view?usp=sharing) in a variable ` df_new`. This file corresponds to new customers who do not yet have categories.\n",
    "- Apply the same transformations as before to obtain a dataframe `X_new` which will correspond to the transformed version of `df_new` (Help yourself from your answer to question t so as not to forget steps )\n",
    "- From X_new and your previously trained model, predict the vector `y_predict` corresponding to the categorization of each of these new customers\n",
    "\n",
    "**Warning**: It is important to keep the same transformations as in training. For example, an imputation by the mean should be imputed by the same mean as in training and not a new mean. Similarly for transformations requiring a `fit_transform`, in the prediction phase only the `transform` is necessary."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 474,
   "metadata": {
    "id": "1abCHpnuHah4",
    "outputId": "42e828c0-1aff-428d-d303-aa6d66cde301"
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "df_new = pd.read_csv(\"customer_segmentation_new.csv\")\n",
    "# print(df_new.info())\n",
    "# print(df_new.describe())\n",
    "#display(df_new)\n",
    "\n",
    "\"\"\" Clean-up \"\"\"\n",
    "# Drop useless columns\n",
    "df_new.drop(columns=[\"hobbies\", \"customer_id\"], inplace=True)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Remove rows with outlier average_price\n",
    "mask = df_new[\"average_price\"] >= 0\n",
    "df_new = df_new[mask]\n",
    "\n",
    "# Fill in null values for average_price, age, gender\n",
    "df_new.average_price.fillna(value=df_new.average_price.mean(), inplace=True)\n",
    "df_new.age.fillna(value=df_new.age.mean(), inplace=True)\n",
    "df_new.gender.fillna(value=df_new.gender.mode()[0], inplace=True)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 475,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "\"\"\" Feature pre-processing \"\"\"\n",
    "# Dummification of country and gender\n",
    "qualitative_features = df_new[[\"country\", \"gender\"]]\n",
    "#encoder has already been fit(), only use transform()\n",
    "qualitative_dummy = encoder.transform(qualitative_features)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Normalization for average_basket, average_price, visit_number and age\n",
    "quantitative_features = df_new[\n",
    "    [\"average_basket\", \"average_price\", \"visit_number\", \"age\"]\n",
    "]\n",
    "#scaler has already been fit(), only use transform()\n",
    "quantitative_scaled = scaler.transform(quantitative_features)\n",
    "\n",
    "X_new = pd.concat(\n",
    "    [\n",
    "        pd.DataFrame(\n",
    "            qualitative_dummy,\n",
    "            columns=encoder.get_feature_names_out(),\n",
    "        ),\n",
    "        pd.DataFrame(\n",
    "            quantitative_scaled,\n",
    "            columns=scaler.get_feature_names_out(),\n",
    "        ),\n",
    "    ],\n",
    "    axis=1,\n",
    ")"
   ]
  },

    "\"\"\" Optimization \"\"\"\n",
    "from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV\n",
    "\n",
    "#params = {\n",
    "#    \"min_samples_split\": [0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5],\n",
    "#    \"max_depth\": [2, 5, 10, None],\n",
    "#}\n",
    "\n",
    "# Let's burn our CPU\n",
    "params = {\n",
    "    \"max_depth\": [2, 5, 7, 10, 15, None],\n",
    "    \"min_samples_split\": [2, 5, 10, 20, 50],\n",
    "    \"min_samples_leaf\": [1, 2, 5, 10],\n",
    "    \"criterion\": [\"gini\", \"entropy\"],\n",
    "}\n",
    "\n",
    "grid_search_clf = GridSearchCV(\n",
    "    estimator=DecisionTreeClassifier(random_state=42),\n",
    "    param_grid=params,\n",
    "    cv=3,\n",
    ")\n",
    "grid_search_clf.fit(X_train, y_train)"
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "# Bonus: définir le modèle final, qui est le plus beau et le plus fort (selon les )\n",
    "\n",
    "# Create the final model, with the best hyperparameters\n",
    "final_model = DecisionTreeClassifier(\n",
    "    criterion='entropy',\n",
    "    max_depth=10,\n",
    "    min_samples_leaf=1,\n",
    "    min_samples_split=2,\n",
    "    random_state=42\n",
    ")\n",
    "# We can use this as well:\n",
    "final_model = DecisionTreeClassifier(\n",
    "    **grid_search_clf.best_params_,\n",
    "    random_state=42\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "# Train the model on all the data\n",
    "final_model.fit(X, y)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Predict new customers type\n",
    "final_predict = final_model.predict(X_new)\n",
    "df_new[\"customer_type\"] = [dict_client_type_mapping[pred] for pred in final_predict]\n",
    "display(df_new)"
   ]
